subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up - latency, throughput, and cost levers
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up - latency, throughput, and cost levers

Alex / Priya - great call earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we can align on SLOs and the cost/performance levers we discussed.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary workload: interactive agent/chat API and multi-turn summarization for Acme's customer support product.
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 latency <= 200ms for single-turn chat responses (streamed), sustained throughput ~100 requests/sec, concurrency up to ~50 concurrent sessions during peak, and streaming support for partial tokens.
- Data residency: US; model variants should avoid PII leakage - will use dedicated tenancy for production.

Questions you raised during the call
1) What levers can we pull to meet p95 200ms while keeping cost reasonable?
2) How does streaming affect latency/throughput tradeoffs?
3) Which quantization/profile options are safe for your quality bar?

Recommended initial configuration (Redwood suggestions)
- Serving profile: low-latency, optimized kernels, prioritizing shorter-sequence execution paths for chat.
- Continuous batching: aggressive continuous batching with dynamic cutoffs for tail-latency control (batch window ~5 ms depending on load). This reduces per-token cost with minimal p95 impact.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts and opening context - expected ~10–25% token savings for multi-turn flows.
- Model variants: use a higher-throughput quantized variant for non-critical/summary workloads and a higher-precision variant for final response generation when quality matters. Fallback routing available if capacity constrained.
- Quantization profiles: start with 8-bit asymmetric (Q8) profiles for search/summary workloads; evaluate 4-bit (Q4) only for offline/regeneration tasks where QA shows no regression.
- Streaming: use chunked streaming with early-first-token emission and continued background decoding to meet perceived latency targets; ensures p50/p90 low while p95 managed via batching windows and priority preemption.

Estimated capacity and cost levers (approx)
- For sustained 100 req/s with avg response ~150 tokens, continuous batching + caching could reduce token compute by ~20–30% vs naive single-request runs.
- Switching to a Q8 quantized variant for ~60% of calls reduces GPU runtime by ~30–40% for those calls; combine with batching for further gains.
- Autoscaling with burst capacity avoids over-provisioning while keeping cold starts low for peak concurrency.

Next steps / asks
1) Please confirm the p95 / throughput targets above (200ms / 100 req/s / 50 concurrency / streaming yes).
2) Share a sample traffic CSV or the peak/minute distribution (you referenced an internal throughput_estimates.xlsx) - attach that and we'll run a quick cost estimate.
3) If you agree, we'll schedule a 45-minute tech deep-dive next week with our infra lead to validate batching windows, kernel selection, and a small perf test plan.

Attachments: throughput_estimates.xlsx (you mentioned this on the call)

Thanks - happy to sync on a time.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-ai.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up - latency, throughput, and cost levers

Thanks Marissa - that looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 200ms p95 is for the first meaningful token in the stream (perceived latency). Total time-to-last-token can be higher for longer responses.
- Average response size: 120–180 tokens; 95th percentile responses can be ~400 tokens.
- We have two traffic shapes: sustained background ~60–80 req/s and spikes to 220 req/s for ~2–5 minute windows.

I've attached the throughput_estimates.xlsx from our load team. Can you run the quick cost estimate and recommend batch/window settings for both sustained and spike scenarios? Also, which quant profiles do you recommend for 95th percentile responses? We need to avoid quality regressions on longer answers.

- Alex
Senior Product Manager, Acme AI
Alex.Chen@acme-ai.com

Attachments: throughput_estimates.xlsx

-----Original Message-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme-ai.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up - latency, throughput, and cost levers

Alex - thanks for the file, received. Quick replies inline:
- Confirmed: p95 target refers to first-token perceived latency; we'll optimize for that with early emission + background decoding.
- For 95th-percentile long responses (~400 tokens) we recommend running generation in two stages: an initial streaming-first-token path on a high-priority lane, then lower-priority background decoding for completion. That keeps perceived latency low while letting longer outputs finish reliably.
- For sustained vs spike: set two autoscaling tiers - baseline pool sized for sustained 80 req/s and a burst pool for spikes up to 250 req/s with pre-warmed instances. Pre-warming avoids cold-start latency.

Recommended quant strategy to avoid quality regression on long answers:
- Production: Q8 for 70% of calls (summary/background), FP16 or mixed-precision for 30% (final generation).
- QA: run A/B evals on a small prompt set including long-answer prompts. We can help run evals (diff BLEU/ROUGE/semantic sim) to validate no regressions.

Batch/window suggestions (initial)
- Sustained: batching window 8ms, target batch size dynamic up to 64 tokens-equivalent depending on queue.
- Spike: batching window 4ms but shift to priority preemption for first-token streaming requests.

I'll put together a short perf-test plan and cost sketch and share by Friday. Want me to include kernel-level optimizations and estimated GPU instance mix?

- Marissa
